_comment: Rungate's own conformity exemptions (#80). Each list is a RATCHET, not a mute: adding an entry that is not a real current violation fails, and an entry that stops being a violation must be removed or the build fails. Shrinking both lists to empty is the work. Consumers get their own file or none at all - these never travel.
_untestedSpecs: DRIFT-2 - testable specs with no test referencing them by name. Over half the testable surface.
_untestedSpecs_310: CONFIG-DIRECTORY-STRUCTURE-SPEC.md is DELISTED as of #310: test/config-reaches-ceremony-tier.test.ts references it and drives the layout it documents all the way to the ceremony-tier decision. This entry carried the note that the spec had to leave the list before SC-478/479 could be rewritten as behavioral assertions; that precondition is now met. The delisting was not a choice - DRIFT-2 ratchets both ways and the build failed on the stale entry, which is the list working.
_untestedSpecs_299: DOC-HYGIENE-ARCHITECTURE-SPEC.md is DELISTED as of #299: test/rules-frontmatter.test.ts references it and drives the frontmatter stamping it now governs, including executing the real DocHygiene hook. Same as #310, the delisting was not a choice - DRIFT-2 ratchets both ways and the build failed on the stale entry the moment a test started naming the spec. That is the list working.
_untestedSpecs_195: INSTRUCTION-COMPLIANCE-SPEC.md is DELISTED as of #195: test/blocking-grades-trust.test.ts names it and drives the blocking-grade refusals it governs, including executing ship.js's own decision block and its AGENT-TIMING block. Same as #310 and #299, the delisting was not a choice - DRIFT-2 ratchets both ways and the build failed on the stale entry the moment a test started naming the spec.
_untestedSpecs_225: The five bootstrap-data-flow entries are NEW to this list and are not new violations: #225 made the spec collectors recursive, so DRIFT-2 can see specs/ subdirectories for the first time. They had been untested since the directory was created and the check was structurally unable to say so. Listing them here banks the visibility; it does not excuse them. Note they are safe to name here precisely because this is not a test file - DRIFT-2 searches test/*.test.ts for a spec's name, so an allowlist living under test/ would have made every listed spec read as referenced.
_untestedSpecs_392: AGENT-BRIEF-TEMPLATE-SPEC.md is DELISTED as of #392: test/agent-brief-template.test.ts now names it, because one of its ids became ambiguous once the registry started reading GATE-CONTRACTS-SPEC.md's heading-form declarations and an ambiguous id can only be claimed from a title that names its spec. Same as #310, #299 and #195 - the delisting was not a choice, DRIFT-2 ratchets both ways and the build failed on the stale entry the moment a test started naming the spec. Worth recording that the trigger was a QUALIFIER rather than a new test: the spec's behaviour was already being driven by that file and only the name was missing, which is the gap the entry had been standing in for. The GATE-CONTRACTS headings have since been renumbered apart, so the qualifier is no longer required to earn that credit - the delisting still stands, because the title still names the spec and the behaviour is still driven, which is what the entry was ever about.
_untestedSpecs_568: bootstrap-data-flow/problem-statement.md is DELISTED as of #568: test/agents-md-sections.test.ts names it and drives the one promise it makes - that the Hard Constraints section of AGENTS.md survives regeneration - through the real scaffold, twice. Same as #310, #299 and #195, the delisting was not a choice: DRIFT-2 ratchets both ways and the build failed on the stale entry the moment a test started naming the spec.
_untestedSpecs_274: CONFIG-DIRECTORY-STRUCTURE-SPEC.md was already DELISTED by #310 before this branch rebased onto it, so #274 removes nothing here. Recorded anyway because #274 adds TWO further independent witnesses: test/consumer-scope-gate-prevalidation.test.ts re-derives every claim the spec's config-expressibility answer makes from source, and test/consumer-ceremony-fixture.test.ts parses its Consumer Config Shape table and asserts the on-disk fixture conforms to it. #310's credit rests on one test file; three independent witnesses survive any one of them being deleted, and DRIFT-2 ratchets both ways, so the entry worth keeping is the one explaining why this spec cannot quietly return to the list.
_untestedSpecs_740: bootstrap-data-flow/consumer-requirements.md is DELISTED as of #740: test/consumer-requirements-ownership.test.ts names it and drives the one claim it had gone stale on - which files the scaffold owns and in what sense - against OWNED_FILES, the declaration .claude/rules/harness-managed.md is generated from. Same as #310, #299, #195 and #568, the delisting was not a choice: DRIFT-2 ratchets both ways and the build failed on the stale entry the moment a test started naming the spec. Worth recording what the entry had been standing in for, because #225 listed these five together and said so - the spec was unreferenced, so nothing could notice that its ownership table had been frozen at the pre-#216 shape for four months while the code moved to five strategies underneath it.
_orphanFiles: HYGIENE-3 - files with zero references anywhere. The two shell scripts may be dead or may be invoked in a way the reference scanner cannot see; that judgement was deliberately not made under a red gate. Resolve each by deleting, archiving to reference/, or referencing it - then delist.
